semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: 'Clinical time series modeling' involves analyzing and modeling data over time within a clinical context. 'Temporal modeling' is a broader term that encompasses the concept of modeling data with respect to time, which is essentially the key aspect of time series modeling.

parent_domains.justification: This domain provides the broader context of analyzing data that changes over time, which is central to the idea of time-series modeling.
Since 'clinical time series modeling' is often about making predictions, this domain serves as a broader parent category that encompasses predictive models in the context of healthcare.
'Clinical time series modeling' is a part of large-scale data analytics in the healthcare sector, making 'healthcare data analytics' a broader category.

closest_parent_domain.justification: The core focus of 'clinical time series modeling' is the analysis of time-indexed data, making 'time-series analysis' the most relevant parent category semantically.

child_domains.justification: 'Time-series forecasting' is a more specific task within time series modeling aimed at predicting future values, often an application of clinical time series modeling.

closest_child_domain.justification: Out of the child domains, 'time-series forecasting' is directly concerned with one of the primary uses of time series modeling - making future predictions - and is particularly relevant in the clinical context for predicting patient outcomes.

sibling_domains.justification: While 'temporal feature modeling' shares the temporal aspect with 'clinical time series modeling', it specializes more in the extraction and utilization of features from temporal data.
This domain shares the predictive aspect of 'clinical time series modeling' and is applied in a closely related domain i.e., public health.
Shares a strong relation to clinical data possibilities, focusing on analyzing clinical data which can include time series.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: 'Temporal feature modeling' is the closest sibling domain as it focuses on aspects of modeling temporal data that are central to time series analysis itself, including in the clinical domain.

unrelated_domains.justification: This area focuses on replicating healthcare processes for training and analysis, not directly related to time series data.
Generative models may be related to creating synthetic data or modeling complex distributions rather than directly working with time-indexed real-world data.
This is a broad field that encompasses many aspects of clinical research and practice, not specifically time series oriented.
